title: 1999 HMMT February Algebra Problem 8
statement: If \(f(x)\) is a monic quartic polynomial such that \(f(-1)=-1, f(2)=-4, f(-3)=-9\), and \(f(4)=-16\), find \(f(1)\).

solutions.text: The given data tells us that the roots of \(f(x)+x^{2}\) are \(-1,2,-3\), and 4 . Combining with the fact that \(f\) is monic and quartic we get \(f(x)+x^{2}=(x+1)(x-2)(x+3)(x-4)\). Hence \(f(1)=(2)(-1)(4)(-3)-1=\mathbf{2 3}\).
